title: Revelation Bible Quiz - Chapter 14
description: Ten questions on Revelation 14: the Lamb on Mount Zion, the three angels with their messages and the harvest of the earth.

questions.text: Where was the Lamb standing with the hundred forty-four thousand?
questions.explanation: The narrator saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with him a number, one hundred forty-four thousand, having his name and the name of his Father written on their foreheads.

answers.text: On Mount Zion
On the sea of glass
On the sand of the sea
On a white cloud

questions.text: What was the sound from heaven first compared to?
questions.explanation: The sound was like the sound of many waters and like the sound of a great thunder, and it was like that of harpists playing on their harps.

answers.text: Like a lion roaring in the wilderness
Like many waters and like a great thunder
Like chariots rushing to war
Like a trumpet and a loud command

questions.text: Who could learn the new song sung before the throne?
questions.explanation: No one could learn the song except the one hundred forty-four thousand, those who had been redeemed out of the earth.

answers.text: Only the twenty-four elders
Only the four living creatures
Everyone standing before the throne
Only the one hundred forty-four thousand

questions.text: What does the text say about those who follow the Lamb wherever he goes?
questions.explanation: These are those who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins; they follow the Lamb wherever he goes and were redeemed by Jesus from among men, the first fruits to God and to the Lamb.

answers.text: They are the two olive trees
They are the prophets of the great city
They are the first fruits to God and to the Lamb
They are the servants sealed at the Euphrates

questions.text: What did the angel flying in mid heaven have?
questions.explanation: The narrator saw an angel flying in mid heaven, having an eternal Good News to proclaim to those who dwell on the earth and to every nation, tribe, language and people.

answers.text: An eternal Good News to proclaim
A golden censer full of incense
A little open book in his hand
Seven last plagues to pour out

questions.text: What did the second angel say?
questions.explanation: The second angel followed, saying, “Babylon the great has fallen, which has made all the nations to drink of the wine of the wrath of her sexual immorality.”

answers.text: That the mystery of God is finished
That the first woe is past
That the hour to reap has come
That Babylon the great has fallen

questions.text: What does the third angel say about the smoke of the torment of those who worship the beast?
questions.explanation: The smoke of their torment goes up forever and ever, and they have no rest day and night.

answers.text: It fills the temple of God
It goes up forever and ever
It darkens the sun and the air
It rises with the prayers of the saints

questions.text: What did the voice from heaven tell the narrator to write?
questions.explanation: The voice from heaven said, “Write, ‘Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on.’” and the Spirit said that they may rest from their labors.

answers.text: “Blessed is he who watches, and keeps his clothes”
“Here is the endurance and the faith of the saints”
“Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on”
“Seal up the things which the seven thunders said”

questions.text: What did the one sitting on the white cloud have?
questions.explanation: The narrator saw one sitting on a white cloud like a son of man, having a golden crown on his head and a sharp sickle in his hand.

answers.text: A golden crown and a sharp sickle
A bow and a crown of gold
A balance and a measuring reed
A golden cup and a seal

questions.text: How far did the blood from the great wine press reach?
questions.explanation: The wine press was trodden outside of the city, and blood came out of it, even to the bridles of the horses, as far as one thousand six hundred stadia.

answers.text: As far as forty-two months’ journey
As far as two hundred million paces
As far as one third of the earth
As far as one thousand six hundred stadia
